texts: Percutaneous closure can be performed for small AP windows: D.
A device can be placed from the groin when the window is small and has rims away from the valves and the coronary arteries.
Most windows are large and are closed surgically on bypass, usually with a patch through the aorta (transaortic) or through the window itself, without circulatory arrest.
The branch pulmonary arteries are mobilized so that they do not kink, and pulmonary hypertensive crises can still occur after repair.
In the picture, the cufflinks brought up the fishing line close the small porthole without a cut.
Memory hook: a small porthole takes the cufflinks from the groin.
